title: Automated spinal-lesion measurements retain an association with neurological recovery
summary: Deep-learning segmentation enabled automatic MRI lesion measurements in 83 spinal-cord injury patients from eight sites. In the observed cohort, lesion width and preserved tissue bridges separated groups with different six-month recovery profiles. These are exploratory within-cohort associations, with no independently validated patient-level prognostic rule or treatment effect.
ai_technology: SCIsegV2 deep-learning segmentation; conditional-inference tree stratification
organization: Balgrist University Hospital; University of Zurich; Polytechnique Montréal

source_review.scope: Read actual primary named segmenter/automatic-measurement operation, clinical cohort/reference, conditional-inference and longitudinal-model Methods, prognostic-association Results and limitations. Prior segmenter training datasets and supplementary code were not independently inspected; no independent validation is inferred. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective eight-site study of 83 patients with clinical MRI and longitudinal neurological assessments. SCIsegV2 automatically segmented lesion and cord masks; geometric processing produced lesion length, width and tissue-bridge measures. Automatic/manual measures correlated at rho 0.540–0.821. Conditional-inference trees fit to 75 six-month outcomes selected lesion width and, for motor subgroups, tissue-bridge width; subsequent longitudinal models described different observed recovery profiles.
evidence.unknown: Outcome-derived thresholds and trajectory comparisons use the same cohort, not an untouched external prognostic test. Segmentation errors, partial-volume effects and imaging timing affect very small bridge estimates. Overlap with prior segmenter development was not independently reconciled; no held-out segmentation validation is claimed. Missing outcomes and heterogeneous care/rehabilitation may confound associations. The study does not establish causal tissue mechanisms, deployable cut-offs or improved treatment.
evidence.ai_role: SCIsegV2 learned image segmentation supplied lesion and spinal-cord masks for automatic morphometrics; learned conditional-inference trees then identified imaging-defined subgroups associated with observed neurological outcomes.
